note: The fuzzer receives the submitted SSML bytes as data and the byte count as size.
The harness allocates a heap buffer exactly one byte larger than the input so it can append a NUL terminator.
The raw input bytes, including the break tag and invalid strength value, are copied into the heap buffer.
The NUL-terminated heap buffer is passed to synthesis with SSML parsing enabled.
The SSML reader recognizes the opening angle bracket from the input as the start of a tag.
The tag body break strength="bogus"/ is copied into xml_buf until the closing greater-than character.

note: The parsed tag body is handed to the SSML tag processor.
The tag name break is resolved to SSML_BREAK, so execution reaches break tag handling.
The strength attribute parser returns a pointer to the user-controlled value bogus inside the tag buffer.
Because the strength attribute exists, the break strength processing branch is taken.
The invalid value bogus matches no mnemonic, so attrlookup returns the sentinel value -1 from the terminal table entry.
The unchecked negative sentinel is stored in value and remains less than zero.
The code only checks that value is below 3, not that it is non-negative, so the invalid -1 proceeds.
Indexing break_value with -1 reads before the local static array, producing an out-of-bounds read under ASan.
